content: Please begin / continue a conversation topic (greetings are not needed). Ensure to change the topic if the current one is losing steam. The conversation should steer towards topics which reveal information about the characters and who they are, or instead drive forward previous conversations in their memory.

Valdr: By the gods, you there! Please, I need help! Spriggans took my friends... I barely made it out alive. Lydia: Spriggans? Ha! Should’ve brought a real hunter, not some milk-drinkers who cry over tree-fuckers. Valdr: Damn it, woman! Niels and Ari are dead in there! I don’t give a skeever’s ass about your Stormcloak bravado right now—I need aid! Lydia: Ugh, fine. But if I have to step into that nasty cave, you better pray to Dibella those twig-bitches don’t make me break a nail. MJR likes my hands smooth for when I— Valdr: Just... do you have a healing potion or not?! Lydia: Relax, twig-boy. MJR’s got plenty. But remember—if you slow us down, I’ll feed your corpse to the next bear we find. Valdr: By Ysmir, you’re insufferable. But if you help me kill those spriggans, I’ll make sure you get first crack at looting their filthy roots. Lydia: Now that’s what I like to hear. Maybe I’ll take one of their heads as a trophy. MJR gets off watching me mount creatures on my greatsword. Valdr: Divines preserve me... just follow me in, and keep your perversions to yourself till we’re done. Lydia: Oh please, like you’ve never fucked a hagraven.
Please wrap up the current topic between the NPCs in a natural way. Nobody is leaving, so there is no need for formal goodbyes.

Valdr: Damn spriggans won’t know what hit ‘em. Let’s move fast—Ari deserves better than rotting in that cave. Lydia: About time we gut some nature-loving freaks. MJR better be watching when I cleave one in half—nothing gets him hotter than blood on my tits. Valdr: ... I’m just going to focus on killing things quietly now. Lydia: Smartest thing you’ve said all day. Now shut up and bleed quietly if you get stabbed. MJR prefers me when I’m not distracted by whining.

I'd almost given up hope of walking away from here. MJR: Who are you?; Valdr: Name's Valdr. I hunt out of Falkreath. MJR: What are you doing out here?; Valdr: We tracked a bear to this den. Good coin for those pelts. We had the big sow cornered when they showed up. Three of them, out of nowhere. Spriggans. Niels went down before we even knew to run. Ari died just inside. I never even thought the things were real. MJR: Why are you still here?; Valdr: I may have lost a drop or two of blood. Truth is, I'm not going anywhere like this. Hurts to breathe. MJR: I may have a potion to spare.; Valdr: I just need a little to get going. MJR: ...; Valdr: Much better. Thanks, friend. I wouldn't have lasted much longer without that. MJR: I understand. Let me help you.; Valdr: You'd do that for a stranger? I don't know what to say. Lead on, I suppose.)

Valdr: I never thought I'd see a spriggan up close, let alone three of them. Those things are nothing like the stories the old hunters tell. Lydia: Stories are for children. You saw the truth of it tonight. Nature's corruption, plain as day. Dibella's domain is beauty and passion, not twisted tree spirits that tear men apart. Valdr: You worship Dibella then? I've always paid my respects to Kynareth for good hunting, but after tonight I might reconsider. Those spriggans felt wrong, like the forest itself was angry. Lydia: Angry because men like you treat it as nothing but a resource for coin and pelts. There's a balance, hunter. The Divines teach us to take only what we need and give thanks. But I suppose thats a lesson lost on Falkreath trappers. Valdr: Easy for you to say, standing there in your fine armor with a housecarl's title. When your belly's empty and the Jarl's tax collector is at your door, you learn to take what you can. Even if it means cracking a few spriggan heads.

Valdr: By the Nine, what was that? Your friend just shouted me across the cave! I was already bleeding from the spriggans, now my ears are ringing too. Lydia: The Dragonborn does as he pleases. If he shouted at you, you probably deserved it. Maybe you got too close to his shot. Valdr: I was standing right here, not moving! He fired an arrow past my head, then that bear came out of nowhere and nearly took my arm off.

Valdr: There's another one! A big one, coming from the shadows! I can barely see it in this darkness. Lydia: Stay behind me, hunter. Let the Dragonborn and I handle this. Dibella's grace guides my blade tonight. Valdr: Your Dibella better guide that greatsword true, because I'm not dying to another tree spirit in one night. My luck's already spent.

Valdr: This one's tougher than the others! I can't get a clear shot with all the branches in the way. Lydia: Then stop whining and find cover! The Dragonborn's arrows will wear it down. Just don't get in his way again. Valdr: Easy for you to say with that greatsword. I've seen what those things can do up close. My bow arm is still shaking from the last fight.

Valdr: Another one of my friends died to these monsters. Niels, Ari, now I'm the only one left. What kind of hunter survives when the others fall? Lydia: The kind who learns from the dead. Your friends are gone, but you're still breathing. That means the Divines have a purpose for you yet. Stop feeling sorry for yourself and help us finish this. Valdr: Purpose?

Valdr: Purpose? I was a hunter, not some hero of legend. Now I'm a man with dead friends and a debt I can't repay. Lydia: You can repay it right now by helping us clear this cave. Every spriggan we kill is one less monster to stalk these woods. The dead don't care about your guilt, only the living matter.

Valdr: You're right. The living do matter. And I'm still alive, so I'll make it count. Point me at the next spriggan and I'll put an arrow through its twisted heart. Lydia: That's the Falkreath spirit I was hoping for. Keep your head down, watch your flanks, and let the Dragonborn do the shouting. We finish this cave, then we get paid.
